q: Under what business model do the dominant credit rating agencies charge the bond issuer rather than investors for a rating?
explain: John Moody originally sold rating manuals to investors (subscriber-pays); in the 1970s the dominant agencies moved to issuer-pays, in which issuers pay for ratings on the securities they wish to sell.

sources.title: Credit Rating Agencies and Their Regulation
sources.quote: By the 1970s, the three dominant CRAs had changed to an "issuer-pays" model, in which a bond's issuer or arranger pays an agency or agencies for initial ratings and for ongoing ratings. The ratings are then available to the public free of charge.

sources.title: SEC.gov | Statement on the Removal of References to Credit Ratings from Regulation M
sources.quote: Credit rating agencies initially used what is referred to as a subscriber-pays business model, meaning that investors paid to access ratings for securities they were interested in purchasing. However, in the 1970s the agencies moved instead to an issuer-pays model, meaning that issuers paid for ratings on the securities they wished to sell.

q: In what year did S&P Global complete its merger with IHS Markit?
explain: IHS Markit completed its merger with S&P Global on February 28, 2022.

sources.title: IHS Markit Form 8-K
sources.quote: On February 28, 2022, IHS Markit Ltd., a Bermuda exempted company limited by shares (“IHS Markit”), completed its previously announced merger with S&P Global Inc. (“S&P Global”).

sources.title: S&P Global Completes Merger with IHS Markit
sources.quote: S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI) ("S&P Global" or the "Company") and IHS Markit earlier today announced the completion of their approximately $140 billion 1 merger, creating a leading information services provider with a unique portfolio of highly complementary assets.

q: Which railcar leasing company created TransUnion as its parent holding company?
explain: TransUnion was created in 1968 as the parent holding company of the Union Tank Car Company, and in 1969 it acquired the Credit Bureau of Cook County.

sources.title: Company History | TransUnion Canada
sources.quote: In 1968, the Union Tank Car Company, a railcar leasing operation, created TransUnion as its parent holding company. In 1969, we recognized an opportunity to grow a new business using our technical expertise. We acquired the Credit Bureau of Cook County (CBCC), which manually maintained 3.6 million card files in 400 seven-drawer cabinets.

sources.title: UTLX History COPY | UTLX
sources.quote: TransUnion Corp. is created as the parent holding company of Union Tank Car Company, Procor and a variety of other businesses.

sources.title: TransUnion - Wikipedia
sources.quote: TransUnion was originally formed in 1968 as a holding company for Union Tank Car Company, making TransUnion a descendant of Standard Oil through Union Tank Car Company. The following year, it acquired the Credit Bureau of Cook County, which possessed and maintained 3.6 million credit accounts.
